about: One ledger for the xMustard-owned process tree (PARITY_REQUIREMENTS §7, §12.4-12.5). Gate v2 (rss_bench_v2.py) attributes every sampled process to a component through process_roles; ledger_check fails a pull request whose measured delta against its base exceeds its workstream's line plus tolerance, grows any other owned component or the owned+external tree, or pushes a process past its §7.2 design line (the cumulative check); `rss_v2.sh ledger` reconciles the design lines, the §7.3 go_daemon items and the workstream lines and exits nonzero while a process is projected over its design line. CI judges a pull request by its base's ledger unless the budget-ledger-change label approves a change. A workstream's designated scenarios outside the CI suite block its pull request on the absolute 95.4 MiB gate only with gate_blocking: true: WS-30 and WS-55, whose acceptance names that gate there, and WS-13, since the overrun on agents-2-small is the per-agent stdio shims WS-13 removes; otherwise only on a regression beyond noise (base median within the gate, head median over it, and both its median and its max more than tolerance.tree_peak_mib above the base's). MiB = 2^20 bytes.

gate.metric: ps-RSS summed over the xMustard-owned tree in one snapshot every 100 ms; externals excluded and reported on their own lines

process_roles.about: Registered roots carry their own component. Descendants are matched by executable name (first matching rule wins; argv1 narrows a rule to a subcommand). Unknown descendants of owned processes count as owned (unclassified:<exe>). External rules and everything below them are never counted in the gate. owned_binaries are pulled in from agent trees: an xMustard binary an agent launched (hook client, shim, relay) counts toward the gate (§12.4 item on hook-client accounting).

rules.note: stdio Go shim; transitional until WS-13 serves MCP over HTTP
per-call core children today; the heavy-slot worker after WS-02/WS-14
compilers, tests, terminals and agent CLIs run by why_failed, diagnostics, verification profiles or runs (§7.6)

sqlite_governance.basis: §7.2: 3-5 steady in-process; the 12 MiB bulk-import peak runs inside the heavy slot

symbol_graph.basis: §7.2 CSR + names; critic: realistic density 180-380 B/symbol

static_embeddings.basis: §7.2, off unless the retrieval gate passes

mcp_access.basis: §7.2: 0 over HTTP; <=3 MiB per stdio relay (each measured stdio Go shim is 8-12 MiB today)

heavy_slot.basis: §7.2 exclusive heavy slot (parse worker, bulk import, index writer, helper)

go_daemon_suballocation.about: §7.3 targets inside the go_daemon design line (unmeasured). Each go_daemon workstream names the item its line lands in (workstreams[].item, WS-10's placement; owners may re-place). A base item's allocation is today's daemon, measured as the reference p50, so lines placed on it are compared at the process level only. Workstreams without an item are unallocated: §7.3 has no room for them.

runtime_base.basis: Go runtime, binary text, HTTP and MCP server base 12-14

sqlite_governance.basis: §7.2 SQLite governance store row (3-5 steady, in-process)

governance_caches.basis: meta, trust tiers, LSH bands, anchor hot set, session-seen sets with TTL <=3

evidence_caches.basis: evidence index, handles, repeat-guard LRU, byte-capped result cache <=2.5

hooks_events.basis: hook handlers, event hub ring (128), progress <=1

run_lineage_runner.basis: run lineage runner idle <=1 (up to ~6 while a run is active, inside peak)

redaction_toolcompat.basis: redaction RE2 set, toolcompat tables, token cache <=1

reconciliation.about: The critic's §12.4 finding stands and is not decided here: the workstream lines overcommit the §7.2/§7.3 design lines. `rss_v2.sh ledger` prints the current numbers (at the Linux reference, base c3603a2 with WS-00 to WS-09 merged except WS-05 and WS-07: go_daemon 21.4 measured, which holds the 5.2 MiB of merged lines, + 22.5 of lines still to merge = 43.9 projected against a 27 MiB design line; rust_index_service 34 of lines still to merge against 32; §7.3 governance caches 10.5 of lines against 3, evidence caches 6.5 against 2.5, hooks 1.5 against 1, runner 2 against 1, and 7 MiB of daemon lines with no §7.3 item; mcp_access 16.6 measured (RSS) with the frozen workload's two stdio shims, and WS-13's -10 leaves 6.6 against a 0 line; rust_core_per_call 9.7 measured with only WS-25's -2 declared against a 0 steady line, although WS-02/WS-14 move per-call work into the resident service) and exits nonzero until the owner decides.
options: raise design lines: the gate cannot absorb the full 16.9 MiB go_daemon overcommit on top of the 87-93 MiB §7.2 peak
cut or re-place workstream lines so every process's lines fit its design line (for example SQLite-resident LSH bands and anchor postings per §12.4, WS-43 opt-in only)
declare offsetting savings as negative lines (§7.2 counts on -3 to -8 MiB from unlinking the platform half; only WS-49's -4 is declared)
reconciliation.enforced_meanwhile: ledger_check's design check fails any pull request whose measured process p50 on a CI-suite scenario is over its design line plus tolerance, and one that takes a process across that line on a designated scenario, so the overcommit fails CI when it materializes, whatever the lines say

WS-65.note: Behind the review build tag, off by default: the default xmustard-api, xmustard-mcp and xmustard-ops builds do not link internal/anchor or internal/review (go list -deps). `xmustard-ops -tags review` is +124 KB of binary; an anchoring runs in that short-lived operator process, measured at 6.7 MB allocated per 50 findings over a 200-file change (BenchmarkReviewAnchor). Worst case at every bound (a diff of 262,144 lines and 8 MiB, 524,288 head lines and 16 MiB, 50 findings found nowhere; BenchmarkPlaceAtTheBounds): 50.3 MiB live, 83 MB allocated and about 0.87 s of CPU per anchoring. WS-66.title: review findings store on the shared govstore tables
WS-66.note: REV-06's figure is 0.5 MiB steady; the line is 0 because nothing in the daemon serves review rows yet: records, triage and re-anchoring run in the short-lived xmustard-ops process under the review build tag, and the store keeps no review cache (the rows live in SQLite, under the page caches sqlite_governance already caps). The default daemon links only the store code and migration 3 (+28 KB of binary). Measured at 50k findings (TestReviewRSSProbe, Linux): serving three times the review rows kept +0.06 MiB of live SQLite and Go heap, inside the 0.5 MiB figure, while settled RSS rose +0.60 MiB, in anonymous pages outside both heaps. WS-67 must re-measure when verify serves review rows from the daemon.

tolerance.basis: Measured 2026-09-25 on darwin-arm64 (Apple M1, 8 GB, shared with other agents, load average 4-55). Tree peak: single v1-workload runs of one set of binaries ranged 66.8-87.9 MiB over 12 runs (the frozen v1's own history is 72.3-84.9 MB); medians of three were 74.2, 78.7 and 80.8 MiB, so CI compares three runs per side and allows 10 MiB. Process check: go_daemon RSS p50 moved 17.8-23.2 MiB within one set of three (lazily reclaimed and compressed pages), footprint p50 11.0-13.1 MiB, so the check uses footprint p50 when both runs report it and allows 3 MiB. Between the medians of two sets of three runs of identical code, footprint p50 moved 2.0 MiB for go_daemon, 1.9 for rust_core_per_call and 4.0 for mcp_access (two stdio Go shims), hence 5 MiB for mcp_access. v1 cross-check: v2 minus the frozen v1 sampler in the same run stayed within 2.33 MiB in 19 of 20 runs and reached -5.62 MiB once at load average 25; it is a gross-error detector (a missed shim or core is 8+ MiB), so it allows 8 MiB. A line smaller than its check's tolerance is below measurement resolution (ledger_check reports BELOW_RESOLUTION, never PASS). Linux check (the reference box, sets of three v1-workload runs of the api-go and rust-core code of feat/parity-v2 c3603a2, load average 5-11): single tree peaks 68.3-81.6 MiB in two clusters (about 69 and 77; the Go daemon's RSS at the peak sample was 21.9 MiB in a low run and 28.9 in high ones), so medians of three ranged 69.1-81.0 MiB over eight sets, beyond the 10 MiB allowance, while the maxes stayed within 75.9-81.6; the tree checks therefore take the smaller of the median and the max deltas (agents-2: medians 80.2-97.1 MiB, maxes 94.8-97.1, over four sets); footprint (PSS) p50 medians moved 1.1 MiB for go_daemon, 0.2 for mcp_access and 0.4 for rust_core_per_call; the v1 cross-check stayed within 1.1 MiB in 11 of 12 runs and reached -5.8 MiB once. Revisit all of these with CI-runner data.

reference_measurement.about: v1-workload (the frozen 501-file workload) measured by gate v2 on Linux, median of three repeats, through the budget-gate job's own commands (the base run of a pull request from parity/ws-10 into feat/parity-v2): binaries built from base_commit, the Rust core from the same tree. component_p50_mib is ps-RSS p50 (the reconciliation projects from it against the RSS-basis design lines); component_footprint_p50_mib is PSS p50, which ledger_check compares a head's footprint p50 with. A process already over its design line here (mcp_access, rust_core_per_call) is bounded on this scenario cumulatively: this p50 + the lines of the workstreams merged into the base after base_commit + tolerance. Those are derived from the first-parent merge commits in base_commit..<base revision> (merge: parity/ws-NN into ..., or GitHub's Merge pull request #N from .../ws-NN); merged_since lists only those merged without a merge commit (squash or rebase). included lists the workstreams already merged at base_commit, whose lines this measurement contains, so the reconciliation does not project them again. Not a GitHub runner: replace this block with the first CI run's base measurement (set base_commit, included and platform; clear merged_since). The previous reference (darwin-arm64 M1, 2026-09-25, base b4f7b49 before any workstream merged) had RSS p50 go_daemon 18.8, mcp_access 20.7, rust_core_per_call 6.2, git_child 0.2 and gate peak 78.7 MiB.
reference_measurement.platform: linux-x86_64 (Ubuntu 26.04, kernel 7.0, procps-ng 4.0.4, 6 cores, 22 GB; shared with a Windows VM and other builds, load average 8-11 during the runs)
reference_measurement.note: rust_index_service (WS-02's resident worker) was not started during this workload at base_commit; mcp_access is two stdio Go shims, whose PSS halves the pages they share
